euromillions.whereToPlay: Portugal, Spain, France, UK, Ireland, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg and Switzerland.
euromillions.history: Born to be the great European transnational lottery. The first draw involved only France, Spain and the UK, but Portugal and others joined in October 2004. Initially stars went up to 9, progressively expanded to 12.

totoloto.format: 5 main numbers (1 to 49) + 1 Lucky Number (1 to 13).
totoloto.history: It is the oldest and most traditional lottery in Portugal. Originally you picked 6 numbers. In March 2011 it adopted the current format with the "Lucky Number", allowing millionaire jackpots to accumulate.

eurodreams.whereToPlay: Portugal, Spain, France, Ireland, Belgium, Austria, Switzerland and Luxembourg.
eurodreams.format: 6 main numbers (1 to 40) + 1 Dream Number (1 to 5).
eurodreams.history: The newest addition to European games. Unlike Euromillions which pays a lump sum, it innovated by focusing on monthly annuities. The 1st prize guarantees 20 thousand euros per month for 30 years.

megasena.format: 6 to 20 numbers from a 60-option ticket (01 to 60).
megasena.history: Created to replace the old Trina, it became Brazil's largest lottery. Besides regular draws, it is famous for the "Mega da Virada" on December 31, which does not roll over and awards hundreds of millions of reais.

hot_numbers.title: How It Works: Hot Numbers
hot_numbers.concept_text: The Hot Numbers system is based on the statistical law of cumulative frequency. It analyzes all registered draws in the database since the first contest and counts how many times each number has been drawn. The premise is that numbers with higher draw frequency in the past maintain a higher tendency to be drawn in the next contests.
hot_numbers.visual_desc: The algorithm counts the total appearances of each number cumulatively.
hot_numbers.range_text: Analyzed History: Since the beginning of the history (draw 1).
hot_numbers.rule_text: Selection Rule: Chooses the most drawn numbers ever.
hot_numbers.rule_history_title: Count: Since the Beginning of History
hot_numbers.rule_history_desc: Analyzes 100% of history. All draws since contest #1 are included.
hot_numbers.rule_recent_desc: Limited moving window. Only recent draws would be counted (does not apply here).
hot_numbers.visual_legend: The highlighted numbers (with the highest scores in the cumulative sum row) are selected by the Hot Numbers algorithm to form its predictions.

recent_numbers.title: How It Works: Recent Numbers
recent_numbers.concept_text: The Recent Numbers system analyzes only a recent window of draws (typically the last X draws). The premise is to detect short-term fluctuations and trends in number outcomes, prioritizing those that are hot in the current trend, rather than analyzing the entire history of draws.
recent_numbers.visual_desc: The algorithm counts the total appearances of each number only within the recent window.
recent_numbers.range_text: Analyzed History: Last X draws (moving window).
recent_numbers.rule_text: Selection Rule: Chooses the most drawn numbers in the recent interval.
recent_numbers.rule_history_title: Count: Since the Beginning of History
recent_numbers.rule_history_desc: Analyzes 100% of history. All draws since contest #1 (does not apply here).
recent_numbers.rule_recent_desc: Limited moving window. Only the last draws are included in the current count.
recent_numbers.visual_legend: The highlighted numbers (with the highest scores in the recent window interval) are selected by the Recent Numbers algorithm to form its predictions.

late_numbers.title: How It Works: Late Numbers
late_numbers.concept_text: The Late Numbers system analyzes the absence of numbers in previous draws. It counts how many consecutive draws each number has gone without being drawn (the delay). The premise relies on Mean Reversion: numbers with high delay accumulate a theoretical probability of appearing soon to balance the long-term statistical distribution.
late_numbers.visual_desc: The algorithm measures the number of consecutive draws in which each number was not drawn.
late_numbers.range_text: Analyzed History: Since the last draw containing each number.
late_numbers.rule_text: Selection Rule: Chooses the numbers with the highest accumulated delay.
late_numbers.rule_history_title: Count: Since the Beginning of History
late_numbers.rule_history_desc: Measures delay based on the history of all draws (does not apply here).
late_numbers.rule_recent_desc: Each draw without appearing adds +1 to the number's delay. When drawn, the delay resets to zero.
late_numbers.visual_legend: The highlighted numbers (with the highest accumulated delay value in the final row) are selected by the Late Numbers algorithm to form its predictions.

markov_chain.title: How It Works: Markov Chain
markov_chain.concept_text: The Markov Chain system models the draw as a state transition process. It analyzes the numbers from the current draw (State N) and calculates the probability of transitioning to new numbers in the next draw (State N+1), based on the historical transition frequency between consecutive draws.
markov_chain.visual_desc: The algorithm builds a transition matrix counting how many times Number B appeared in the draw immediately following Number A.
markov_chain.range_text: Analyzed History: Transition between all consecutive draws.
markov_chain.rule_text: Selection Rule: Chooses the numbers with the highest average transition probability from the previous draw's numbers.
markov_chain.rule_history_desc: The starting point is the set of numbers drawn in the latest draw.
markov_chain.rule_recent_desc: Calculation of each number's appearance probability based on the sum of all transitions from the source numbers.
markov_chain.visual_legend: The numbers with the highest transition probabilities calculated from the last combination are selected by the Markov Chain.

clustering.title: How It Works: Clustering
clustering.concept_text: The Clustering system uses machine learning algorithms (K-Means) to group past draws into clusters with similar mathematical properties (e.g., total sum, odd/even counts, etc.). By predicting which cluster the next draw should belong to, the algorithm suggests the numbers that are statistically dominant (centroids) within that group.
clustering.visual_desc: The algorithm classifies each historical draw into a cluster and calculates the Euclidean distance of numbers to the cluster center.
clustering.range_text: Analyzed History: All draws grouped into K clusters.
clustering.rule_text: Selection Rule: Chooses the numbers closest to the center of the projected cluster.
clustering.rule_history_desc: Identifies which group has the highest cyclical probability of appearing next.
clustering.rule_recent_desc: Orders numbers by distance to the centroid of the selected cluster.
clustering.visual_legend: The numbers closest to the geometric center of the chosen cluster (with the lowest Euclidean distance) are selected by the Clustering algorithm.

pyramid_pascal.title: How It Works: Pyramid Pascal
pyramid_pascal.concept_text: The Pyramid Pascal system builds a continuous sum digital pyramid. 1) We start at the base with the units digits of the last draw (e.g., 12, 31, 17, 26, 43 -> base: 2, 1, 7, 6, 3). 2) We add adjacent pairs using Modulo 10 Arithmetic (e.g., 7 + 6 = 13 -> keeps 3; 3 + 8 = 11 -> keeps 1) from bottom to top, generating a total of 15 digits in the structure. 3) We count the frequency of each digit (0 to 9) in the entire pyramid. 4) Each lottery number (1 to 50) is scored by summing the weights of its two individual digits (e.g., Number 23 receives the weight of digit 2 + weight of digit 3). The numbers with the highest combined score are suggested.
pyramid_pascal.visual_desc: The pyramid is generated by adding adjacent pairs modulo 10. The count of all 15 digits generated across all layers dictates the final score of numbers from 1 to 50.
pyramid_pascal.range_text: Analyzed History: Relies exclusively on the last draw to generate the pyramid.
pyramid_pascal.rule_text: Selection Rule: Extracts patterns and sequences from the digits generated in the upper layers.
pyramid_pascal.rule_history_desc: Base digits come directly from the recently drawn numbers.
pyramid_pascal.rule_recent_desc: Successive additions create new numeric layers with oscillatory behavior.
pyramid_pascal.visual_legend: The system counts the frequency of digits 0-9 across all layers of the pyramid. Then, it scores each number (1 to 50) by summing the weights of its two digits (e.g., Score of 23 = Frequency of 2 + Frequency of 3). The top voted (highlighted) are suggested.

pyramid_gaps.title: How It Works: Pyramid Gaps
pyramid_gaps.concept_text: The Pyramid Gaps system analyzes the mathematical intervals (gaps) between sorted drawn numbers. 1) For each historical draw, it sorts the numbers and calculates the 4 intervals between them (e.g., draw 3, 10, 22, 28, 42 -> intervals: +7, +12, +6, +14). 2) The system counts which starting numbers and which intervals are most frequent in history. 3) It crosses the 5 most common starting numbers with the 5 most common intervals of each position to generate valid theoretical combinations. 4) All numbers belonging to these frequent combinations are suggested.
pyramid_gaps.visual_desc: The algorithm calculates the distance (difference) between consecutive numbers of each historical draw to map the most recurring intervals.
pyramid_gaps.range_text: Analyzed History: All historical draws to calculate gap frequencies.
pyramid_gaps.rule_text: Selection Rule: Rebuilds numbers from the sum of the most likely gaps over frequent starting numbers.
pyramid_gaps.rule_history_desc: The starting point of the combination (first drawn ball).
pyramid_gaps.rule_recent_desc: The most common statistical distances between consecutive balls.
pyramid_gaps.visual_legend: We map the most common distances between balls. By combining the most common starting points with these frequent intervals, the system generates likely combinations and suggests the numbers that make them up.

monte_carlo.title: How It Works: Monte Carlo
monte_carlo.concept_text: The Monte Carlo system uses statistical modeling to simulate thousands of virtual draws (in this case, 1000 simulations). 1) First, it calculates the historical draw probability of each number. 2) In each simulation, it performs a weighted draw of 5 numbers based on those historical probabilities using a seeded random number generator (Seeded RNG). 3) It counts the number of times each number was drawn across all 1000 simulations. 4) The numbers that appear most frequently in the simulations are suggested.
monte_carlo.visual_desc: The algorithm executes 1000 simulations of virtual draws weighted by historical frequency and accumulates the results.
monte_carlo.range_text: Analyzed History: All historical draws to calculate probabilistic weights.
monte_carlo.rule_text: Selection Rule: Chooses the numbers with the highest accumulated count in 1000 simulated draws.
monte_carlo.rule_history_desc: Base frequency of numbers in actual history (weight probability).
monte_carlo.visual_legend: We simulate 1000 draws based on the probabilities of each ball. The numbers with the highest frequency of appearance in the simulations (highlighted) are suggested by the system.

media_3_otimizado.title: How It Works: Trimmed Mean 3 Optimized
media_3_otimizado.concept_text: The Trimmed Mean 3 Optimized system predicts numbers by analyzing position trends in drawn balls. 1) For each of the 5 number positions (Ball 1 to Ball 5), it analyzes the last 10 draws. 2) It removes the lowest and highest values for each position (Trimmed Mean) to eliminate one-off anomalies. 3) It calculates the arithmetic mean of the remaining values for each position. 4) It suggests the average number obtained (Tier 0) and its two immediate neighbors (+1 and -1, Tier 1). In case of a tie, it prioritizes numbers with higher recent frequency.
media_3_otimizado.visual_desc: The algorithm independently calculates the trimmed average of the last 10 appearances of each ball, suggesting the average and its immediate neighborhoods.
media_3_otimizado.range_text: Analyzed History: Last 10 draws to calculate the average of positions.
media_3_otimizado.rule_text: Selection Rule: Chooses the average calculated per position (Priority 1) and its two neighbors (+/- 1, Priority 2).
media_3_otimizado.rule_history_desc: Arithmetic average of appearances removing the extremes (outliers).
media_3_otimizado.rule_recent_desc: Immediate adjacent numbers to the mean to prevent small amplitude variations.
media_3_otimizado.visual_legend: For each drawn ball (1 to 5), we remove the minimum and maximum of the last 10 draws and calculate the average. The average (Tier 0) and its adjacent neighbors (+1 and -1, Tier 1) are suggested.

universal_oscillation.title: How It Works: Universal Oscillation V2
universal_oscillation.concept_text: The Universal Oscillation V2 system is based on the theory that the Digital Roots of drawn numbers tend to oscillate (change groups) from one draw to the next. 1) It calculates the Digital Root (continuous sum of digits until 1 digit remains, e.g., 39 -> 3+9=12 -> 1+2=3) for each number. 2) It determines the dominant (most frequent) root in the last draw. 3) It assigns a base weight using the numbers' frequency in the last 1000 draws. 4) It applies the Oscillation Rule: numbers with a NON-dominant root receive a 1.5x score Boost, while numbers with the dominant root of the last draw are penalized by 0.5x. The highest-scoring are suggested.
universal_oscillation.visual_desc: The algorithm penalizes the dominant root of the last draw and rewards the remaining alternative roots to simulate natural probabilistic oscillation.
universal_oscillation.range_text: Analyzed History: Last 1000 draws to calculate base frequencies.
universal_oscillation.rule_text: Selection Rule: Applies a 1.5x Boost to alternative roots and a 0.5x Penalty to repeating roots over historical frequencies.
universal_oscillation.rule_history_desc: Reduction of a number to the sum of its digits (e.g., 14 -> 1+4 = 5).
universal_oscillation.rule_recent_desc: Score adjustment to force statistical dispersion of consecutive roots.
universal_oscillation.visual_legend: We identify the digital roots of the last draw. Candidates with a non-dominant root gain a 1.5x Boost, while those with the dominant root are penalized (0.5x). The numbers with the highest adjusted scores are suggested.

diagonais_da_matriz.title: How it Works: Matrix Diagonals
diagonais_da_matriz.concept_text: The Matrix Diagonals system identifies 45° geometric flows in the historical draw matrix. 1) For each candidate number, we trace two diagonals starting from the cell directly above (the previous draw). 2) The left diagonal rises towards number 1; the right diagonal rises towards the maximum number (e.g., 50). 3) We sum the number of times draws fell along these diagonals up to a depth of 50 past draws. This ensures a balanced analysis of exactly 50 cells for every candidate number. The numbers with the highest sum are recommended as they represent the strongest geometric resonance lines.
diagonais_da_matriz.visual_desc: Visualization of the left and right diagonals rising from the target number, intersecting the historical draw matrix.
diagonais_da_matriz.range_text: Analyzed History: Last 50 draws (maximum diagonal depth).
diagonais_da_matriz.rule_text: Selection Rule: Chooses numbers whose accumulated diagonals contain the highest number of historical hits combined.
diagonais_da_matriz.rule_history_desc: Sums of left and right diagonals bounded by the matrix edges (1 to 50).
diagonais_da_matriz.rule_recent_desc: The sum of the lengths of both diagonals for any number always totals 50 unique cells.
diagonais_da_matriz.visual_legend: We trace diagonals upward from the target number. Each circle represents a historical hit found on the corresponding diagonal. The sum of both determines the final score.

diagonais_da_matriz_3d.title: How it Works: 3D Matrix Diagonals
diagonais_da_matriz_3d.concept_text: The 3D Matrix Diagonals system extends geometric analysis by rolling the draw matrix into a virtual cylinder (where column 50 connects to column 1). 1) Diagonals rise from (T-1, N) without physical edge limitations. When a diagonal reaches column 1 or 50, it continues on the opposite side. 2) The scan is not limited to 50 draws; it traverses the entire history of draws since draw #1. 3) We sum the accumulated historical geometric hits. The numbers with the highest score represent the three-dimensional diagonal lines with the greatest accumulated continuous frequency.
diagonais_da_matriz_3d.visual_desc: Visualization of the 3D diagonal tubular flow with continuous wrap-around effect from the latest draw back to draw #1.
diagonais_da_matriz_3d.range_text: Analyzed History: 100% of historical draws since the start of the database.
diagonais_da_matriz_3d.rule_text: Selection Rule: Chooses numbers with the highest accumulated score along cylindrical diagonals across the entire history.
diagonais_da_matriz_3d.rule_history_desc: Diagonals cross matrix boundaries and restart on the opposite edge.
diagonais_da_matriz_3d.rule_recent_desc: Calculations performed over 1900+ draws to maximize three-dimensional accuracy.
diagonais_da_matriz_3d.visual_legend: By rolling the matrix into a tube, the left and right diagonals flow continuously without stopping at the edges. The system scans the entire history from draw 1 and recommends numbers corresponding to the lines with the highest accumulated resonance.

RespGaming.intro1: At <bold>Números Mágicos</bold>, we love numbers, patterns, and probabilities. However, there is a number more important than any lottery combination: <bold>your limit</bold>.
RespGaming.intro2: We want your experience on this site and in the game to be <bold>positive and fun</bold>. Therefore, always keep the following principles in mind:
RespGaming.rule1Desc: The statistical analysis we present serves to increase the interest and strategic fun of the game. <bold>It should not be seen as a way to guarantee income or solve financial problems</bold>.
RespGaming.rule1Box: The probability of winning the jackpot remains <bold>1 in 139,838,160</bold>.
RespGaming.rule2Title: 2. The Past does not predict the Future
RespGaming.rule2Desc: Mathematically, the game is of <bold>"independent draws"</bold>. The fact that a number has been drawn 10 times in the last year or has not been drawn for 50 draws, <bold>does not guarantee it will be drawn or fail in the next</bold>.
RespGaming.rule2Box: Our tools help identify trends, but <bold>not certainties</bold>.
RespGaming.rule3Title: 3. Only play what you can afford to lose
RespGaming.rule3Desc: Set a <bold>strict budget</bold> for gaming and never exceed it.
RespGaming.rule3Box: ⚠️ Never use money intended for essential expenses (housing, food, bills) to place bets.
RespGaming.rule4Desc: Gambling for money and the use of betting platforms are <bold>strictly prohibited for minors under 18</bold>.
